content: <thought>The mass spectrum shows a dominant ion at m/z 180.0423, which in positive‑mode ESI is most likely the [M+H]⁺ adduct. Subtracting the proton mass gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈179.035 Da. Considering the isotopic pattern (≈10 % M+1, ≈1.3 % M+2) suggests a molecule with about 7–9 carbons and several oxygens, but no halogens. A formula that matches the neutral mass within a few ppm and reproduces the observed isotope pattern is C₇H₉O₄ (exact monoisotopic mass = 157.0501 Da). If the observed ion is instead the [M+Na]⁺ adduct, the neutral mass would be ≈157.053 Da, which aligns very closely with C₇H₉O₄. Therefore the most consistent molecular formula is C₇H₉O₄.
